info.name: LedgerOne - Accounting (Ledger / General Ledger Read Model)
info.description:
General Ledger read-model submodule API collection (Get Account Ledger, Get Ledger by query, Get Ledger Entry drill-down). Reflects the implementation exactly as shipped in apps/api/src/shared/accounting — read-only, no create/update/delete endpoints exist for the Ledger at all (00_BUSINESS_RULES.md Ch.19.18: only the Journal Entry posting process may create Ledger Entries). Does not modify or duplicate FinancialYear/FiscalPeriod/ChartOfAccounts/JournalEntries.postman_collection.json — this collection creates its own Account Group/Account/Financial Year/Fiscal Period/Journal Entry fixtures as Setup steps, posting three Journal Entries to build a genuine three-row Ledger history (500, then +100, then +100) to page through.

Design note (JWT required): same convention as every other collection in this folder — every protected request carries `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`, the same long-lived (10-year) RS256 dev-only token for tenantId 900001 already used by FinancialYear/FiscalPeriod/ChartOfAccounts/Currency/Tax/JournalEntries.

Design note (repeatability): a collection-level pre-request script generates `{{lgYear}}` (base 8000, distinct from every other collection's own base/modulus sharing the same financial_years/accounts tables under the same companyUuid) once per Newman invocation, mirroring JournalEntries.postman_collection.json's own established trick.

Design note (cursor pagination, PAG-001..005): the 'Get Account Ledger' folder's three 'Page N of 3' requests chain a real, server-minted opaque cursor across three separate HTTP requests via `pm.collectionVariables` — this is the definitive proof that keyset pagination never skips or duplicates a row and that the running balance carries forward correctly across page boundaries (a bug in exactly this continuity was caught and fixed during this milestone's own live verification before this collection was finalized).

Design note (Ledger is read-only, structurally): no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE route exists anywhere under `/ledger` — there is nothing to test for those methods because Express itself has no such route registered (Ch.19.18), not merely a permission check.

Run order for a full pass, top to bottom: every 'Setup' request must run first, in order, to seed fixture variables; every non-setup request depends on them. The three 'Page N of 3' requests within 'Get Account Ledger' must also run in order (each depends on the previous one's own `nextCursor`).
